name: Tullius Sabinus
bio: Tullius Sabinus is one of the epigrammatists whose short poems were gathered in the Greek Anthology. Paton's index of authors gives no firm date for the poet. Paton's index lists the poet among the writers of the Wreath of Philippus, the Garland compiled in the first century AD.
This archive carries the 1 epigram ascribed to the poet in the third volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Book IX: 410).

poems.title: Book IX, 410
poems.author: Tullius Sabinus
poems.text: A mouse once, lickerish of every kind of food and not even shy of the mouse-trap, but one who won booty even from death, gnawed through Phoebus’ melodious lyre-string. The strained chord springing up to the bridge of the lyre, throttled the mouse. We wonder at the bow’s good aim; but Phoebus uses his lyre, too, as a weapon wherewith to aim well at his enemies,
